goals.title: From tissue scans to results
goals.description: A whole-slide scan is too large to work with as one image. I broke it into tissue cores, smaller patches and individual cells, then tested which view best matched expert staining grades and supplied lymphoma subtype labels. Each result can be traced back to where it came from.
path: Turn whole scans into traceable cores, patches and single cells (point-and-click halved core marking time from 6 s to 3 s; WebP cut patch storage by 86.5%).
Compare autoencoders, Barlow Twins contrastive learning and frozen pretrained encoders to represent patches compactly.
Test core, patch and cell features against expert IHC grades on grouped folds (patch scale reached 0.238 MAE vs 0.382 inter-assessor gap).
Pool patch bags to predict ABC vs GCB subtypes (UNI patch features reached 0.970 accuracy / 0.992 AUC; 2D positions gave no patch-scale gain).
Project model scores back onto tissue coordinates, test dimming controls, and trace figures to raw predictions.
figure: Schematic showing one scan and one selected core branching into patches and cells.
Synthetic schematic. The patch and cell views both come from core C01. The thesis crop was 5,000 × 5,000 pixels, covering 1.25 × 1.25 mm at the reported scan scale (Table 2.5, p. 70).
start: Why I chose 1-click cropping (6 s → 3 s)
Trace Case S02 to the grading chart
See what the subtype results support
files: Frames the three-scale thesis hypothesis across image preparation, expert staining grades and molecular subtype prediction.
Provides one copyable command to rerun the end-to-end grading workflow and inspect the generated CSVs and SVG figure.

title: 1. Prepare tissue scales
summary: Before testing any model hypothesis, multi-gigabyte whole-slide scans had to be turned into uniform cores, background-filtered patches and segmented single cells that fit on disk and kept their exact scan coordinates.

goals.title: Locate tissue cores
goals.description: Can we locate every tissue core on a whole-slide scan in half the manual time without losing accuracy or crop uniformity?

story.tried: 4 core-finding methods (Hough, 2-click grid, drawn boxes, 1-click fixed box).
story.found: Point-and-click took 3 seconds per core instead of 6 for rectangles. Both found all the target cores in the comparison and made no wrong selections. The grid was faster but could clip off-centre cores. Hough missed more cores.
story.next: Adopted 1-click fixed-size (5,000 × 5,000 px) cropping across all 1,109 cores.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Table 2.5, p. 70, and August 2020 annotation scripts.

files: 1.00 precision/recall at 6 s/core, with uneven pixel dimensions across hand-drawn boxes.
0.5 s/core and 1.00 recall from 2 corner clicks, dropping to 0.98 precision when cores drift off the grid line.
3 s/core and 1.00 precision/recall using 1 centre click and a fixed square crop (shifting inward at edges).
Thesis Table 2.5 comparing speed, precision, recall and manual effort across all 4 core extraction methods.
Saves point centres and rectangle bounds to a portable CSV manifest before pixel extraction.

goals.title: Extract traceable crops
goals.description: How do we cut out each marked core so downstream patch and cell predictions can always be placed back on the full scan?

story.tried: Saved each core crop alongside a CSV manifest of scan origins and 4× downsample factors.
story.found: Scan = Origin + Scale × Local mapped any reduced crop box back to exact full-scan pixels.
story.next: Fed traceable cores into patch tiling (#patches) and single-cell segmentation (#cells).

files: Cuts out one image per marked region and writes crops.csv linking filenames to source scan coordinates.
Converts a 20 × 20 px box on a 4× downsampled crop back to its 80 × 80 px full-scan coordinates.

goals.title: Tile into patches
goals.description: How do we tile each core into regular squares while discarding empty glass background and catching cores with zero usable patches?

story.tried: Tiled full core bounding boxes, applied ≥ 50% Otsu tissue filtering, and logged 0-patch cores.
story.found: Retained 229,683 tissue patches (207 ± 61/core) while catching empty/damaged cores before training.
story.next: Saved accepted patch images with core IDs, pixel bounds and tissue coverage fractions.

files: Computes tissue coverage per grid square and keeps only squares meeting the ≥ 50% tissue threshold.
Counts retained patches for every expected core, keeping 0-count cores visible to flag missing tissue.
Writes accepted patch images and a patches.csv manifest with source core, bounds and tissue fraction.

goals.title: Segment single cells
goals.description: Can we extract millions of individual cells with their scan coordinates and check whether a few cores dominate the cell count?

story.tried: Size-filtered Cellpose instances, indexed global scan (x, y) coords, and audited per-core cell counts.
story.found: Across 9,126,415 cells, per-core counts varied sharply (8,229 ± 3,664; 75% in 1 core in demo).
story.next: Enforced ≥ 1,000 cells/core and ≤ 220 px diameter gates for cell-scale grading and subtyping.

files: Extracts size-filtered 8 × 8 px cell crops from segmented instances while rejecting tiny specks or clumps.
Adds each cell's local offset to its core origin to record exact full-scan (x, y) coordinates.
Packs aligned cell IDs, coordinates and features into one compressed archive with verified row order.
Reports cell counts, median cells per core and largest-core share (75% in demo) plus 0-cell cores.

goals.title: Compress & audit storage
goals.description: How can we shrink 229,683 patches enough for repeated training runs and catch corrupted dataset shapes before jobs launch?

story.tried: Compared PNG and WebP in the thesis. The public examples separately check a generated patch, dataset structure and local read times.
story.found: In the thesis, WebP reduced storage for 229,683 patches from 26.94 GB to 3.63 GB (86.5%). The generated patch example measures a separate pixel difference.
story.next: Stored patch and core collections in WebP and ran pre-flight array audits before GPU jobs.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 2 results, p. 72 and Fig. 2.12.

table.title: Storage depends on collection scale
rows: PNG header smaller on 1 tiny smooth image
table.note: Always benchmark storage on the real image collection rather than a single synthetic tile.

files: Measures byte size and decoded RGB channel difference for PNG vs WebP on the same patch.
Flags missing files, unexpected spillover files and mismatched array shapes before training starts.
Times reading 12,288 identical bytes from 20 separate files versus a single contiguous bundle.

title: 2. Compress into features
summary: Training multi-scale models directly on raw pixels is expensive. This section tests three ways to turn image patches into compact feature vectors—autoencoder reconstruction, self-supervised Barlow Twins, and frozen pretrained backbones—while keeping every vector linked to its scan coordinates.

goals.title: Autoencoder reconstruction
goals.description: How much visual detail is retained when a patch is squeezed through a narrow numerical bottleneck and reconstructed?

story.tried: Fitted AE/VAE bottlenecks across widths, ranked worst-MSE patches first, and split pixel BCE from β·KL loss.
story.found: Doubling code width (16 B → 32 B) cut MSE 2.9× (0.00141 → 0.00049), but pixel reconstruction produced unseparated UMAP clouds (0.015 sil.).
story.next: Tested self-supervised Barlow Twins (#features) and frozen pretrained backbones (#frozen-features).

files: Compresses 3-value patches into a 2-number latent code and reconstructs the inputs.
Ranks held-out samples worst-first by mean squared error so high-residual cases are inspected first.
Measures the trade-off between code byte size (16 B vs 32 B) and held-out MSE across bottleneck widths.
Separates pixel reconstruction error (0.387) from the β-weighted KL code penalty (0.5 × 0.083 = 0.042).

goals.title: Contrastive view learning
goals.description: Can a shared encoder learn features that stay invariant across two augmented views of a patch without collapsing into redundant columns?

story.tried: Trained a shared encoder on paired augmented views with Barlow Twins invariance + off-diagonal redundancy loss.
story.found: Off-diagonal penalty (+0.010) blocked duplicate columns; 40 steps cut loss 0.1938 → 0.0003 (thesis Silhouette 0.408 vs 0.015 AE).
story.next: Audited learned matrices for zero-std or correlated columns before downstream grading and subtyping.

files: Shows how off-diagonal redundancy penalises duplicated feature columns even when view agreement is 0.000.
Applies random horizontal flips and brightness gains to produce two views linked by the same patch ID.
Flags zero-variance (collapsed) columns and near-duplicate correlated column pairs (|r| ≥ 0.99).
Updates one shared weight matrix over 40 steps, reducing the Barlow Twins objective from 0.1938 to 0.0003.

goals.title: Pretrained encoders
goals.description: How do we standardise histology patches for frozen pretrained backbones and compare their vector footprints?

story.tried: Standardised RGB resize/normalisation, extracted frozen backbone vectors in ID-ordered batches, and compared 16-D vs 64-D footprints.
story.found: Batch extraction preserved exact patch ID order while shrinking 30 patches to 1,920 B (16-D) or 7,680 B (64-D).
story.next: Benchmarked frozen ResNet-50 and UNI vectors alongside learned features (#feature-benchmarks).

files: Extracts one feature vector per patch in batches while keeping patch IDs in their exact input order.
Compares in-memory float32 byte footprints (1,920 B vs 7,680 B) across 16-D and 64-D encoders on 30 examples.
Resizes RGB images and normalises channels to the target mean and standard deviation expected by a fixed encoder.

goals.title: Benchmark feature quality
goals.description: Which feature representations group related examples cleanly and detect rare positive instances inside a multi-patch bag?

story.tried: Compared encoders on held-out centroid accuracy, Silhouette separation, 2D PCA variance and 64 planted-signal MIL bags.
story.found: When 1 of 12 patches carried the positive signal, max pooling reached 0.999 AUC vs 0.830 for mean pooling (which diluted the signal).
story.next: Carried instance-sensitive attention/max pooling into Task 1 grading and Task 2 subtyping.

files: Compares candidate feature sets on the exact same held-out test split (100% vs 50% accuracy in demo).
Computes per-sample silhouette scores (0.85–0.87) comparing within-group vs nearest other-group distance.
Projects 3D feature vectors onto 2 principal axes explaining 97.8% and 2.2% of variance.
Shows max pooling (0.999 AUC) beating mean pooling (0.830 AUC) when 1 of 12 patches in a positive bag carries the signal.

goals.title: Keep vector coordinates
goals.description: How do we guarantee that cached feature vectors stay aligned to their exact source patch coordinates even if files are reordered?

story.tried: Exported vectors with (l, t, r, b) bounds, joined tables by region_id across shuffled rows, and checked cache metadata.
story.found: ID-keyed joins recovered exact coordinates regardless of file order, and pre-flight checks caught encoder/shape mismatches.
story.next: Used coordinate-linked feature caches for scale grading (#grading-models) and spatial heatmaps (#heatmaps).

files: Writes each feature vector beside its region_id and (left, top, right, bottom) pixel bounds.
Joins region coordinates and feature vectors by ID across reordered inputs and flags any missing IDs.
Verifies cached vector shape, encoder name and ID ordering against the experiment specification.

title: 3. Task 1: Staining grades
summary: Hypothesis test 1: how closely can models trained on cores, patches or single cells reproduce expert immunohistochemical (IHC) staining grades (0–3), and how does model error compare with the disagreement between human assessors?

goals.title: Reference grades & splits
goals.description: How do we combine multiple assessor ratings into a reference grade while keeping related samples together in the same validation fold?

story.tried: Averaged assessor grades per core while logging rater count (n) and spread, and assigned grouped validation folds.
story.found: Logging n alongside spread separated two agreeing raters (n=2, spread=0) from 1 uncorroborated rating (n=1, spread=0).
story.next: Trained core, patch and cell graders on identical group-aware cross-validation folds.

files: Computes mean reference grade alongside rating count (n) and rater spread (max − min).
Assigns sample groups to folds so related samples (g1: a, b) never cross the train/test boundary.

goals.title: Compare scale graders
goals.description: Which biological scale—whole core, tissue patch or single cell—most accurately reproduces expert staining grades on held-out cases?

story.tried: Trained core, patch and cell graders on shared splits, saved out-of-fold predictions, and broke down signed bias by grade.
story.found: Patch features reached the lowest thesis grading error (0.238 MAE vs 0.278 cell and 0.346 core).
story.next: Compared the 0.238 patch MAE directly against human inter-assessor disagreement (0.382) in #agreement.

files: Fits separate scale models on shared training IDs and compares predictions on the same held-out sample.
Writes out-of-fold predictions alongside reference grades so every case is scored unseen.
Breaks error into signed bias (+0.45 at Grade 0 vs −0.55 at Grade 3) and absolute error by ordinal grade.

goals.title: Matched ablation runs
goals.description: How do we test one training change at a time fairly—and catch runs where a startup setting silently differed from the plan?

story.tried: Paired baseline and single-change runs by fold/seed, audited startup logs, and averaged fixed final-epoch windows.
story.found: Matched pairing isolated exact trade-offs (−43.9% time, −35.0% RAM, +3.1% error) and startup checks caught silent config drift.
story.next: Applied verified single-change schedules across the 81-run grading and subtype ablations.
story.source: Submitted thesis, Chapter 3, Fig. 3.4 and Appendix A.2.

files: Pairs runs by fold and seed to report mean % change in error (+3.1%), time (−43.9%) and memory (−35.0%).
Expands baseline and single-parameter variants across shared folds and random seeds (12-run grid).
Flags runs where an effective startup setting differed from the plan or was absent from the log.
Compares mean balanced accuracy (0.760 vs 0.770) and elapsed time (66 s vs 51 s) over a fixed final epoch window.

goals.title: Sample rare & hard cases
goals.description: Can dynamic sampling revisit rare grades and high-loss examples during training, and how does the model respond to out-of-distribution noise?

story.tried: Combined class rarity, training loss and EMA weights for dynamic sampling, and probed the 8th null class with Gaussian noise.
story.found: In the generated examples, weighting gives rare or difficult grades more chances to appear. The toy classifier labels all 12 noise bags and none of the 12 signal bags as outside its expected inputs.
story.next: Evaluated trained grading error alongside human inter-assessor disagreement (#agreement).

files: Combines inverse class frequency, training loss and previous weights (Appendix A, Algorithm 3).
Compares null-class probability on generated signal bags (0.009 median, 0/12 calls) vs noise bags (0.683, 12/12 calls).

goals.title: Model vs expert gap
goals.description: How does the model's grading error compare with the disagreement between two human experts scoring the same tissue?

story.tried: Measured person-vs-person |A − B| gap alongside model-vs-consensus MAE and quadratic-weighted κ.
story.found: Human assessors differed by 0.382 grade points on average, while the patch model differed from their consensus mean by 0.238.
story.next: Reported both metrics together with distinct targets (person-vs-person vs model-vs-mean).

files: Computes assessor-to-assessor gap (0.50 in demo; 0.382 in thesis) alongside model-to-consensus MAE (0.15 in demo; 0.238 in thesis).
Computes quadratic-weighted κ (0.90 on 4 paired grades), penalising multi-grade jumps more heavily than 1-grade misses.

title: 4. Task 2: Subtype labels
summary: Hypothesis test 2: can multiple-instance learning over patch or cell representations predict the supplied ABC and GCB molecular subtype labels—and does adding 2D spatial patch positions or hierarchical pooling improve accuracy relative to compute cost?

goals.title: Curate subtype cohort
goals.description: Which specimens had valid ABC or GCB subtype labels, required stains and sufficient tissue patches to enter the comparison?

story.tried: Joined image IDs to {'ABC', 'GCB'} calls without inferring missing labels, and logged every exclusion gate per core.
story.found: 6-gate filtering (cell ≤ 220 px, patches ≥ 87, cells ≥ 1,000, rater Δ ≤ 1, slide check) curated 1,109 cores down to 962 (86.7%).
story.next: Held the 962-core curated cohort fixed across all pooling, positional and encoder comparisons.

files: Matches image IDs to allowed {'ABC', 'GCB'} labels and flags unrecognised or missing entries for review.
Records pass/fail status across label, required-stain and minimum-patch rules for each specimen.

goals.title: Pool patches per case
goals.description: How should hundreds of patch vectors from one specimen be combined into a single case-level subtype prediction?

story.tried: Compared mean, max and softmax-attention bag pooling, size-sorted variable bags, and scored held-out bags.
story.found: In generated examples, attention gives patches different weights. Sorting four bags by size reduces padding from 19 slots to 5 (about 74%).
story.next: Tested whether 2D spatial patch coordinates or cell-to-patch hierarchy improved bag predictions (#subtype-ablations).

files: Compares mean, maximum and softmax-attention summaries on the same 3-patch bag.
Sorts specimens by patch count before batching to minimise masked dummy padding slots.
Fits a bag-level centroid classifier on training specimens and scores held-out specimen bags.

goals.title: Test position & hierarchy
goals.description: Does giving the transformer 2D spatial patch coordinates or pooling cells within patches first improve subtype prediction?

story.tried: Ablated 2D rotary position encodings (RoPE) on identical patch bags and compared flat cell vs patch-then-core pooling.
story.found: In the generated example, using 2D positions changes the pooled score from 0.500 to 0.369. The thesis reports no clear patch-scale subtype advantage from adding positions.
story.next: Preserved this negative result in the logbook and recommended testing on intact whole-slide tissue (#limits).

files: Isolates the effect of 2D rotary position encoding on a pooled attention score (0.500 off vs 0.369 on) while masking padded slots.
Shows why flat cell averaging (0.25) weights dense patches more heavily than hierarchical patch-then-core averaging (0.50).

goals.title: Cross-fold ROC & recall
goals.description: Which subtype representation performed best across validation folds, and how do class recalls behave across thresholds?

story.tried: Evaluated fold-by-fold subtype accuracy, tie-aware ROC AUC and per-class recall (k/n) across 3 validation folds.
story.found: Patch · UNI reached 0.970 accuracy and 0.992 macro AUC in internal validation. Macro AUC was 0.958 for Patch · ResNet, 0.952 for Cell · ResNet and 0.675 for Core · Contrastive.
story.next: Reported explicit per-fold denominators and scoped need for multi-centre external validation (#limits).
story.source: Submitted thesis, Table 4.4, p. 161, and limitations, p. 190.

table.title: Best-performing subtype model in Thesis Table 4.4
table.note: External multi-centre validation is required to test generalisation across laboratories and scanners.

files: Reports fold-by-fold grading MAE (0.25, 0.30) and subtype accuracy (100%, 50%) so weak folds are never hidden by averages.
Traces true vs false positive rates across score thresholds (handling tied scores at 0.60) to compute ROC AUC (0.875).
Reports ABC and GCB recall per fold alongside explicit correct/total counts.

goals.title: Accuracy vs compute cost
goals.description: Which models sit on the Pareto frontier when we weigh subtype accuracy against runtime, peak memory and storage?

story.tried: Compared raw RGB vs cached float32 vectors, filtered models on the 3D Pareto frontier, and audited timing/RAM logs.
story.found: 256-D vectors shrank 500 regions 147× (75.26 → 0.51 MB), and Pareto filtering dropped models beaten on accuracy, time and RAM.
story.next: Carried Pareto-efficient representations into spatial heatmap and perturbation analysis (#heatmaps).

files: Shows 500 regions shrinking from 75.26 MB (224 × 224 RGB) to 0.51 MB (256-D float32 vectors).
Identifies undominated Pareto-frontier models (wide, small) and drops candidates beaten on all three axes (slow).
Flags runs with missing memory logs or absent run records before plotting compute trade-offs.

title: 5. Explain & verify
summary: A high validation score is not enough for scientific workflows: researchers need to see which tissue regions drove a prediction, test whether dimming those regions changes the score more than a uniform control, and trace every published figure back to verified run outputs.

goals.title: Spatial score heatmaps
goals.description: How do we project model scores back onto the source tissue image while clearly marking regions that were never scored?

story.tried: Projected patch scores onto core grids, averaged overlaps, and rendered shared-scale heatmaps with hatched NaN areas.
story.found: Hatching unscored (NaN) pixels prevented background glass or skipped tissue from being misread as a 0.0 score.
story.next: Paired visual heatmaps with ROI coverage receipts and dimming controls (#explain).

files: Places patch scores onto a 4 × 3 coordinate grid, averaging overlaps (0.60) and marking uncovered cells as NaN.
Renders a shared-scale heatmap over a 64 × 48 px image with overlapping patches averaged to 0.55 and unscored areas hatched.
Reports scored ROI coverage (2 of 3 points, 66.7%), median score (0.60) and range (0.40–0.80).

goals.title: Dimming & perturbation
goals.description: When an explanation highlights part of a tissue image, does dimming or removing that region change the score more than a uniform control?

story.tried: Fitted Spectral Dream Dimming masks, tested targeted vs uniform dimming at equal 0.80 brightness, and ran leave-one-out probes.
story.found: Targeted dimming dropped the score 3.5× more than uniform dimming (−0.576 vs −0.164), confirming spatial model sensitivity.
story.next: Separated network sensitivity from biological causation, which requires wet-lab assays (#limits).

files: Fits separate bounded brightness masks for Class A and Class B against a fixed model.
Sets out how to test explanation masks with controls and why biological meaning requires separate evidence.
Compares targeted spatial dimming (Δ −0.576) against a uniform control mask at identical 0.80 mean brightness (Δ −0.164).
Measures class score shifts when removing each patch vs repeating only that patch.

goals.title: Schedule & resume jobs
goals.description: How do we give every cluster experiment a deterministic ID and resume interrupted jobs without repeating committed work?

story.tried: Hashed canonical JSON specs into 16-hex SHA-256 run IDs and saved completed chunks atomically to disk checkpoints.
story.found: Deterministic IDs blocked duplicate jobs, and atomic checkpoints resumed interrupted runs from the last committed chunk.
story.next: Reconciled finished cluster outputs against the manifest before building tables (#run-results).

files: Expands 2 configs × 2 folds × 2 seeds into 8 jobs with deterministic SHA-256 run IDs.
Commits completed chunks atomically so an interrupted run reuses [4] and recomputes only unfinished chunks [9, 16].

goals.title: Audit completed runs
goals.description: How do we catch missing, crashed or duplicate runs before aggregating fold metrics into a result table?

story.tried: Guarded result merges against duplicate (config, fold, seed) keys and audited job states against the run manifest.
story.found: Separating 'missing metrics' (crashed mid-run) from 'missing' (never launched) pinpointed log checks vs resubmissions.
story.next: Passed only complete, verified run matrices to the figure and table builders (#figures).

files: Merges result CSVs by (configuration, fold, seed) and rejects duplicate keys before averaging.
Compares planned jobs against observed states to flag runs with missing metrics or no run record.

goals.title: Reproduce thesis figures
goals.description: Can a reviewer start from one error bar in a results figure and trace it all the way back to the individual case, fold and raw ratings?

story.tried: Replayed the 12-case grading workflow end-to-end, traced Case S02 across 3 scales, and verified assets with SHA-256 hashes.
story.found: Patch scale reached the lowest error (0.216 MAE vs 0.371 cell, 0.464 core), with Case S02 traceable back to ratings (2, 3).
story.next: Run python run_grading_example.py --output grading-demo and verify report checksums.

files: Aggregates out-of-fold predictions into per-scale MAE summaries after checking sample alignment.
Renders per-scale MAE summaries directly into a clean, reproducible SVG bar chart.
Replays the full grading workflow on 12 synthetic cases, tracing Case S02 from ratings (2, 3) to the final chart.
Bins per-core patch counts into half-open intervals [0–49, 50–99, 100–199, 200+] for distribution figures.
The rendered 3-scale grading error chart produced from the 36 synthetic held-out predictions.
Computes SHA-256 fingerprints for expected report tables and flags any missing figure files.

goals.title: Study limits & next tests
goals.description: What do the internal single-cohort comparisons establish, and what would a multi-centre external study need to test next?

story.tried: Evaluated all grading and subtype models across 3-fold cross-validation within the main clinical TMA cohort.
story.found: Internal CV establishes agreement within this cohort and scanner; it does not prove generalisation to external hospitals.
story.next: Pre-register fixed weights and preprocessing rules, then test across independent multi-centre cohorts.

files: Summarises what internal validation supports and specifies the requirements for external multi-centre validation.

title: 6. Appendix: PCam benchmark
summary: To test the multiple-instance bag pipeline on an external public dataset, this appendix assembles repeatable positive and negative patch bags from PatchCamelyon (PCam) and compares frozen encoders on fixed bag splits.

goals.title: Assemble benchmark bags
goals.description: How do we group patches into repeatable positive and negative bags with fixed seeds so different encoders face the exact same benchmark?

story.tried: Assembled seeded positive bags (1 pos patch in 4) and negative bags (0 pos) with disjoint train (11) and test (23) seeds.
story.found: Locking bag manifests and patch IDs on disk guaranteed identical splits across every candidate encoder.
story.next: Fed the fixed bag manifests to candidate encoders in Compare bag encoders (#pcam-benchmarks).

files: Generates reproducible 4-patch positive and negative bag manifests for train (seed 11) and test (seed 23) splits.

goals.title: Compare bag encoders
goals.description: When we hold the train/test bag manifests and max-pooling rule fixed, how clearly does the benchmark separate a signal encoder from noise?

story.tried: Scored a signal encoder and a random-noise encoder on the exact same 8 train and 8 test bags using max pooling.
story.found: Signal encoder reached 1.000 balanced accuracy vs 0.625 for the noise encoder on identical bags.
story.next: Verified the MIL bag benchmark pipeline before comparing pretrained histology backbones.

files: Compares two encoders on identical train/test bag manifests using max pooling and balanced accuracy (1.000 vs 0.625).
